mempool_public.meaning: pending buyBack() transactions targeting V3 pools are observable in the public mempool before execution

amount_out_minimum.meaning: amountOutMinimum parameter set by the V3 _performSwap path

sqrt_price_limit_x96.meaning: sqrtPriceLimitX96 parameter set by the V3 _performSwap path

post_swap_validation_present.meaning: whether the V3 swap path performs post-swap validation (report states it does not, unlike V2)

swap_executes_at_inflated_price.meaning: the V3 buyback swap executes at an arbitrarily inflated price rather than being rejected by effective slippage protection

every_v3_buyback_exploitable.meaning: every V3 buyback is exploitable, undermining the buyback-and-burn mechanism

assumptions: The attack relies on a standard MEV sandwich technique and public mempool visibility (as_mev_technique).
buyBack() is callable without an authorization requirement; the report does not state a caller restriction.
The attacker's front-run buy and back-run sell may be separate transactions; the report does not specify.

unresolved.description: Report gives no exact OLAS amounts or fair-value comparison values, so the magnitude of value loss cannot be numerically bound; only the qualitative inflated-price execution is encoded.
Exploitability is conditional on public mempool visibility; a private mempool is noted as a possible mitigation, so the 'every V3 buyback' universality is scoped to the public-mempool scenario.

limitations: The impact i_repeatable is a potential/universal claim; the plan encodes it as a per-buyback Boolean under the public-mempool scenario rather than a quantified universal over all buybacks.
No numeric slippage bound or fair-value reference is supplied, so the relation uses grounded Booleans for the inflated-price execution and repeatable exploitability.
Code-level binding of amountOutMinimum=1 and sqrtPriceLimitX96=0 to the actual _performSwap call is deferred.
